bib.title: A Primer in Post-Training Reasoning Data: What We Know About How It Works

legacy_report:
SOURCE: "A Primer in Post-Training Reasoning Data: What We Know About How It Works", Yaoming Li, Guangxiang Zhao, Qilong Shi, Lin Sun, Xiangzheng Zhang, Tong Yang (Peking Univ., Tsinghua, Qiyuan Tech). arXiv:2606.02113v1 [cs.CL], 1 Jun 2026. Preprint, no venue printed. The file is li-2026-primer-post-training-reasoning-data.pdf.

COVERAGE: 22 of 22 pages read. Main text is pp.1-9, references pp.9-17, appendix pp.17-22 (all read). I read the references only for origins. The extraction was clean text. Figures were not rendered, so I know them only from captions.

NATURE: This is a pure survey of "over 150 key public studies". It has no experiments, no datasets, no models and no numbers of its own. Its original contribution is a framework: a taxonomy, an attribution ledger and "release fields" checklists. The PDF has no headline accuracy numbers. The only numeric items are "150 papers", the scaling equations, and DAPO's "accuracy 0 or 1" filter. Every empirical finding is restated from other papers.

CLAIMS (all restated; origin in parentheses)
1. Data difficulty is base-relative. A problem can be unreachable for one base, useful for another and saturated for a third. DAPO drops prompt groups whose accuracy is 0 or 1, and Skywork-OR1 estimates difficulty per model. Bears on note 08 and note 06.
 number: none (accuracy 0 or 1 is a filter rule).
 setup: Origins are Yu et al. 2025 (DAPO), He et al. 2025a (Skywork-OR1) and Hochlehnert et al. 2025. The primer ran no tests.
 quote: "Skywork-OR1 estimates difficulty against model variants, while DAPO implements the same idea by removing prompt groups with accuracy 0 or 1" (p.4)
2. Small curated sets (LIMO, s1) work only when the skill is already in the base policy's support. Big pools matter when the useful gradients sit in the tail or must cover several bases or domains. Bears on note 08 (how little data) and note 05.
 number: none.
 setup: Origins are Ye et al. 2025 (LIMO), Muennighoff et al. 2025 (s1), Yue et al. 2025 and Wu et al. 2026. OpenThoughts (Guha 2025) and Big-Math (Albalak 2025) are the large-pool counterpoint.
 quote: "few demonstrations can elicit strong behaviour only when the skill already lies within the base policy's support" (p.5)
3. RLVR may only sharpen what the base can already do. Counter-literature relaxes this with ProRL (longer horizon), RL-PLUS (external rollouts), CoT-Pass@K (a different metric) and PASS@(k,T) (interaction depth). So "RL expands capability" depends on which assumption was broken. Bears on note 08 and note 05 (SFT vs RL).
 number: none.
 setup: Origins are Yue 2025, Wu 2026, Liu 2025, Dong 2026, Wen 2025 and Zhai 2026.
 quote: "Yue et al. (2025) and Wu et al. (2026) read current RLVR as sharpening trajectories already accessible to the base policy." (p.7)
4. Scaling decomposition. A is the reachable ceiling and B (or k(N)) is approach efficiency. Data substrate, verifier and context move the ceiling. Loss design, sampling and warm-start distillation move efficiency. Data total = D_unique × τ (reuse). The authors say the equations are a "reading device", not a universal law. Bears on note 06 and note 08.
 number: R(C)=R0+(A−R0)/(1+(Cmid/C)^B); D_total=D_unique×τ.
 setup: Origins are Khatri et al. 2025 (large-scale RL runs) and Tan et al. 2026 (Qwen2.5 dense series).
 quote: "Tan et al.'s decomposition Dtotal = Dunique × τ makes reuse part of the scaling surface rather than a preprocessing detail" (p.7)
5. Coverage is a recipe, not a count. Source mixture, filter, teacher and generator choices decide what is inherited. Synthetic data can narrow recursively, carry hidden teacher traits and leak benchmarks. Bears on note 06.
 number: none.
 setup: Origins are Guha 2025 (OpenThoughts ablations), Xu 2025b (Structure Trumps Size), Shumailov 2024, Cloud 2025 and Han 2025.
 quote: "Coverage is a recipe, not a count." (p.4)
6. Reward channels are brittle. LLM judges can be fooled by trigger tokens, math accuracy collapses under surface changes, rule verifiers false-reject, and learned verifiers can be hacked. Co-evolving generator and verifier increases the need for versioning. Bears on note 08 (reward) and note 06.
 number: none.
 setup: Origins are Zhao 2025b (master-key), Mirzadeh 2025 (GSM-Symbolic), Huang 2025 and Shao 2026b (spurious rewards).
 quote: "LLM judges may reward trigger tokens, math accuracy may collapse under surface changes, rule verifiers can false-reject, and learned verifiers can become hackable" (p.8)
7. Self-play does not remove curation. It moves curation into an "anchor": answer, interpreter, majority vote, role split or archive. STaR, R-Zero, Absolute Zero and TTRL are the examples. Pseudo-label accuracy can degrade as generated tasks get harder.
 number: none.
 setup: Origins are Zelikman 2022, Huang 2026a, Zhao 2025a and Zuo 2025.
 quote: "Self-play does not eliminate curation; it moves curation into the anchor that turns generated behaviour into trainable feedback." (p.6)
8. Agent data should be replayable episodes. Cleaned SFT success traces remove failures, retries and state diffs, which are where credit assignment is visible. Table A3 lists 10 audit fields. Bears on note 06 and note 05.
 number: none.
 setup: Origins are Pan 2025 (SWE-Gym), Trivedi 2024 (AppWorld), Xie 2024 (OSWorld) and Qin 2023.
 quote: "Clean SFT traces often remove failed actions, retries, recoveries, and sibling rollouts—the branches where credit assignment is visible." (p.2)
9. Long CoT is not faithful reasoning. Traces can rationalize or copy teacher style. Process supervision (PRM800K, Math-Shepherd, OmegaPRM, PRIME) varies in where its signal comes from, and PRMs need testing (ProcessBench, PRMBench). Bears on note 05.
 number: none.
 setup: Origins are Turpin 2023, Lanham 2023, Lightman 2023, Wang 2024, Luo 2024, Zheng 2025 and Song 2025.
10. Frontier recipes converge on the same scaffold: long-CoT SFT or distillation, then RLVR with GRPO-style optimization. Examples are DeepSeek-R1, Kimi K1.5, Qwen3, Magistral, Phi-4-reasoning and Llama-Nemotron. Distill-then-RL buys cold-start speed. Pure RL cuts teacher inheritance but depends more on the verifier and prompt support. "Optimizer visibility is not causal isolation." Bears on note 05 (SFT vs RL).
 number: none.
 setup: Primer pp.5-7. Causal attribution is not tested.

Table 1 (p.2) lists eight "traps" with a "Future Reporting" checklist. Examples are base model, rollout count, temperature, pass-rate band, verifier version, teacher, decontamination status and inference budget.

BASELINES/ABLATIONS: None of its own. Ablations are only referred to (OpenThoughts, Guha 2025).

LIMITS (authors' own, p.9): Closed pipelines and proprietary mixtures are absent. It is "question-driven rather than a formal meta-analysis". The evidence is a mix of peer-reviewed papers, preprints, tech reports and model cards, used "to document public recipes and release practices, not to establish causal rankings". It says "we do not independently re-run training recipes, audit contamination, or validate every verifier". Appendix A.1 says non-peer-reviewed sources are not used to settle causal claims. Citation-heavy, with little detail per claim. It cites many 2026 works that I could not check.

BUILDS ON: Lightman 2023, Wang 2024 and Luo 2024 (process supervision). Guha 2025 (OpenThoughts). Yu 2025 (DAPO). Khatri 2025 and Tan 2026 (scaling). Yue 2025 and Wu 2026 (RLVR support). Ye 2025 and Muennighoff 2025 (small sets). DeepSeek-AI 2025a (R1).

CODE: none.

FIGURES (from captions, not rendered):
- Fig 4 (p.4) "Quality support matrix": correctness, difficulty, trace quality and coverage each need different evidence.
- Fig 5 (p.4): useful difficulty lies between always-fail and always-pass.
- Fig 7 (p.7): ceiling versus efficiency.
- Fig 8 (p.8): small versus large pool coverage.

PROBLEMS: No embedded instructions found. Figures were not inspected. The appendix holds no results, only tables A1-A4 (inclusion lens, source clusters, trajectory audit fields, source placement). A.8 discloses ChatGPT use for language polishing only.

Verbatim quotes with page numbers (as requested): p.4 "Coverage is a recipe, not a count."; p.5 "few demonstrations can elicit strong behaviour only when the skill already lies within the base policy's support"; p.6 "Self-play does not eliminate curation; it moves curation into the anchor that turns generated behaviour into trainable feedback."

Suggested handling: the paper sharpens notes 06 and 08 on base-relative difficulty, small-set limits and the brittleness of reward. It cannot be cited for any measured number. Cite the origin papers for those.
